writeup: We’ve got a newcomer in the top spot to start the season! I completely love Kyle’s first five rounds of the draft. First, getting CMC at the 9th spot is an absolute gift, then to follow that up with Hampton, Nabers, Egbuka, and Warren is a drafting dream come true. Gainwell and Mason are great RBs to have on the bench, and he has Hunter Henry just in case Warren’s injury concerns linger. My only concern is he lacks a top QB, but if either Purdy or Love can play consistent football it won’t matter too much.

The reigning Delaware Champion is poised to make a great run once again. Hugh’s championship prize is Jahmyr Gibbs, a player set for a historic season. On top of that he’s got a lot of great WRs and Brock Bowers, who’s a great asset despite his price. Hugh will have a new QB, and although Caleb Williams isn’t quite Josh Allen caliber, he’s got all the weapons to be an explosive player this year. His depth behind Gibbs is a bit concerning, though. Jaylen Warren is his RB2, and I’d say there’s a 50/50 shot he loses the bulk of the carries in Pittsburgh to Rico Dowdle. If that does happen, Hugh will have a hole that needs addressing if he wants to stay near the top of the league. My favorite pick by Hugh this year is De’Zhaun Stribling in the 10th round. He’s a great sleeper pick to put at the bottom of an already strong roster.

“Of course the guy writing the power rankings puts himself in the top three.” Well, yeah. Jokes aside, Bijan could very well be the best fantasy player in a year without a clear number one going into the season. Garrett Wilson managed to fall slightly to my third round pick, and he’s the only tried and true WR1 you can get at that price. Colston Loveland being there in the 5th was a steal, getting a top TE in an otherwise poor round. Bo Nix in round 11 was circled on my chart as the best value-for-money QB in the draft considering the Bronco’s scheme and his history. My one glaring weakness is a lack of a bonafide WR2. Williams, Washington, and Godwin Jr all look good on paper but none of them are top targets on their teams. If all three of them somehow bust, my team will definitely drop in the rankings.

Greg didn’t have much of a choice when Ja’Marr Chase was available at the 6th pick of the first round. He took Jeremiyah Love in the second, a high-upside rookie who could be a real star at RB this year, although he comes with injury concerns. He’s got plenty of depth behind him though, taking RBs in rounds 4-6 after drafting Olave as his WR2. He also waited until near the end of the draft to grab Kyler Murray, a QB with rushing upside with big boom potential. His only weakness is depth at WR considering he only drafted 4, but as of now Greg’s got an incredible squad.

I had a feeling AJ Brown would be a hot commodity in this year’s league, so Brady getting him with the 20th pick to partner Puka is a great move. He might have a weak spot at RB considering his RB1 is a Jet and the Giants backfield might be too crowded to allow for another electric Skattebo season, but Brady took advantage of a sliding TreVeyon Henderson to add some depth at the position with a potential RB1 for New England.

Johny went all in on WR. No one has more depth than him at the position after he took 5 of them in the first 8 rounds. He secured Achane and Jayden Daniels as well, adding star power at other positions. Unfortunately, Jacory Croskey-Merritt sticks out like a sore thumb as his RB2. Last year’s preseason darling didn’t live up to the hype as a rookie, but maybe he’ll be serviceable this season. Either way, waiting until the 10th round to pick a starting RB is a risky strategy, but no one is more poised to make a roster-defining trade that Johny right now.

Quinn took the best available RB in each of the first three rounds. Unfortunately, one of those RBs is Josh Jacobs, who was placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt List and will be ineligible to play for an undisclosed amount of time. Some reports have even suggested that he may never play again. He’s stacking his WR1 Ladd McConkey with Justin Herbert, a smart strategy as long as his QB locks in and stops playing kissy-poo on the practice field with his super hot fiancé. Kincaid in the 11th round is also a great value pickup and allowed him to address every other position early in the draft.

Jorge had one objective this draft: get JSN. He might’ve had to reach to get him at 1.03, but he got his guy. He had a balanced approach for the next few rounds, making sure to cover his RBs and WRs before picking up LaPorta in the 7th. Jorge had a pretty safe draft overall, but outside of JSN, I don’t see a player that jumps out as a difference maker.

Jackson might sneakily have the best WR trio in the league with CeeDee, Flowers, and Odunze. I’m personally high on Flowers, and think he could be a potential league winner as a third round pick. Of course the Ravens fan made sure to stack his favorite offense by drafting King Henry as well, but he leads what I believe to be a subpar RB group with Judkins and Jonathon Brooks. Burrow was a value pick at QB, and Jaxson Dart has the potential to be the highest scoring QB for some weeks this year. If his RBs can show consistency, this will be a great team.

Honestly, Camden’s got a good team. I liked him getting Jefferson in the second round, and it’s great to see many-time Delaware Fantasy champion Josh Allen not being on Hugh’s team. There are a few question marks in his draft strategy though, taking three TEs in rounds 5, 7, and 10, as well as a defense in round 9. Even if this is finally Pitts’ year, having Goedert and Andrews waste away on the bench won’t do him any favors. Considering his RB2 is Rhamondre Stevenson, it might’ve been better had he taken a few extra RBs in case the Patriots decide to favor Henderson this year.

I’ve never in my life seen an auto draft go so poorly. He’s got 3 QBs, used a 2nd rounder on a TE, and made a risky pick with Jeanty at 1.04. However, the team’s not all bad, as Rashee and Davante Adams could be an electric WR duo, and he’s bound to have a strong QB week after week with Hurts, Dak, and Mahomes being his options.

The preseason power rankings have never been kind to Rick, but he usually proves me wrong. I don’t have him much worse than the rest of the league this year, but there are a few too many weaknesses he has to address post-draft. He lacks a WR1, as his top three WRs are Higgins, Burden III, and Mike Evans. His RB duo is questionable, has he took Saquon and Javonte Williams with his first two picks. They’re great players, but he reached to get them on his team. He did secure a great QB in Drake Maye, but I’m afraid he paid too high a price for the team he has for me to be excited.

With Jahmyr Gibbs, Caleb Williams, and Christian Watson all scoring over 30 points, Hugh was able to secure a blowout victory over Johny. Unfortunately, sleeper WR Stribling went down with an ankle injury and is expected to miss at least a month, which makes two injured players for Hugh already.

No RB duo scored more this week than Bijan and Kenneth Walker’s 65 points. Their performances allowed my squad to win by a large margin despite Loveland’s goose egg. If the Loveland hype was just smoke, this team could have a massive hole to address.

Massive week for Quinn. Chase Brown was the lowest scorer of his four active RBs with 18.8 points. Even with questions surrounding Josh Jacobs’ return to football, Quinn’s got a squad that could be able to fill his absence for the long term.

Brock Purdy had a good game, but that was about it for the former top ranked team. CMC and Hampton both disappointed and he lacks a backup capable of replacing them if either have a bad year. It’s too soon to overreact, but Kyle’s team might need some extra juice to reclaim the top spot in the rankings.

Jorge had the highest scoring squad with 158.64 points. He narrowly edged out Luke after a tense Monday Night Football game. The Dream Dwerkers were led by huge games from Swift, JSN, and Nico Collins, and 19 points from the Steelers’ Defense. The Steelers don’t play Cooper Rush every week though. Courtland Sutton was frustratingly absent from the Bronco’s offense, so Jorge might be looking for new options at flex.

Harrison Butker vaulted Camden to victory over Jackson, finishing off a great week with solid outings from every position. Josh Allen balled out and vintage Justin Jefferson emerged with Carson Wentz under center. Camden had two of his three TEs in the starting lineup, but unfortunately one of them was Kyle Pitts, who scored nada.

Greg was the lowest scorer this week with a dumbfounding total that rounds up to 88 points. When your QB goes down and combines with your DEF and K for less than a single point, you’re not going to score all that much. Kyler’s concussion is unfortunate, but Shough played well on Greg’s bench. Greg also had solid output from Bucky Irving and Olave, which shows that he should still have a decent squad assuming his luck improves.

The Little Beauties couldn’t finish the comeback against Jorge, but there’s a lot to like about this team. Jeanty played like a league winner, and Hurts, Montgomery, and McBride all had big games. Unfortunately, none of Luke’s WRs broke 10 points, so he clearly has a need to address if he wants to be a contender.

The first game of the season left Brady heartbroken after news broke that AJ Brown will be hitting the IR due to a high ankle sprain. He was still able to beat Rick, but the rest of the season looks shaky until his second round pick recovers. Luckily for him, Coker exploded for 34 points on his bench. Perhaps he has a replacement ready to go.

Johny couldn’t beat Hugh this week despite a nearly 30 point performance from St. Brown. Achane was subpar and Harrison only managed 4 points. His Daniels/JCM duo might not have filled the stat sheet, but 17 touches for the RB in Week 1 is a sign of big upside in the coming weeks.

Jackson lost by a field goal to Camden despite Henry and Flowers combining for over 60 points on their own. Unfortunately, Zay Flowers injured his hamstring and the only notable performances on the bench came from Jackson’s two backup QBs.
It was a rough week for Rick. Five of his first six draft picks all failed to score double-digit points. Rick made a lot of reaches in the draft, so if this continues he may be in deep trouble.

Thanks to huge games from Jonathan Taylor and Kincaid, Quinn was able to squeak past Brady in a low-scoring game. Just because he’s the new #1 doesn’t mean he’s got a perfect team though. Herbert is his only QB and ranked 27th at the position, he’s still missing Josh Jacobs, and Terry McLaurin will be without his quarterback for a few weeks.

9 catches for 155 yards and 3 touchdowns is a statline that Jorge’s gonna be swooning over for years to come. The Dwerkers’ star player JSN led his team to a strong win with his 42.5 points. In support, LaPorta and Kyren had good games as well. Unfortunately, Price and Sutton have been busts so far, and Jorge’s bench doesn’t look very well equipped to replace them.

Ja’Marr in combination with Shough and Olave was an unstoppable trio for Greg. The Saints’ offensive explosion late in their game was the deciding factor in what was otherwise setting up to be a close game against Last Chance U. Greg might be looking for a RB going forward, though, as Etienne and Love have both been disappointing so far.

Colston Loveland has found himself on Academic Warning at Last Chance U. Back to back stinkers from the 5th rounder combined with a 2 catch game from Jamo made it impossible for me to win, even if the Falcons didn’t pull Bijan in the third quarter. However, Kenneth Walker and Parker Washington still exploded, and newly-acquired Bryce Young popped off for another 3 TD game on the bench.

I mean no disrespect by ranking ESPN’s top team 5th, but in a week where Josh Allen and James Cook combine for over 60 points, Camden should’ve scored more than just 113. Running the goalline formation somehow worked again despite his two TE’s combining for 3.9 total points. Camden will be enjoying his share of the Bills’ offense all season, but he needs more support from his other players if he wants to be the top dawg.

Hugh almost came back against Camden’s 60 point lead going into Sunday, but he couldn’t overcome what turned out to be an offensive implosion. Caleb Williams’ hamstring injury makes 5 hurt players on Hugh’s roster, but 3rd rounder Brock Bowers is on track to return to the field this week. He’ll need more than just Gibbs to score him points going forward, so hopefully Bowers has an instant impact.

The Little Beauties had another great week. Despite my original pessimism for the auto-drafted team, Luke might have a real squad here. 138.86 points made him the highest scorer of the week thanks in part to Davante Adams’ 39.5. His RB’s failed to produce much this week, but it’s too early to know if that continues or if they’ll go back to what they did in Week 1.

It was a great bounce-back week after his devastating loss to Camden in Week 1. Jackson seamlessly replaced injured Zay Flowers with Rashod Bateman’s 21.8 points, and Bateman should prove to be a great pickup if Zay’s injuries persist. Jackson will have a few too many injuries taking up spots on his bench for the next few weeks, so he might have to make some tough roster decisions soon.

Brady would be 2-0 if he knew Puka wouldn’t play before Monday. Despite the late inactivity, he still mustered a decent week, but much of his points came from his kicker. Kelce’s big game was a nice surprise, and TreVeyon hit the ground running in his first game of the season. Jalen Coker also proved he might be one of the steals of the season with his second 8 catch game already.

Draft day champion Kyle might not have what it takes. Malik Nabers had his shoulder popped out and will be playing with a backup QB for the rest of the season according to my sources. Purdy and CMC continue to be bright spots on the team, but the further you scroll down his roster, the sadder you get.

Johny’s opponents have scored almost 300 points in just two weeks. Big games from St. Brown, DeVonta Smith, and Tet almost prevented him from going 0-2. Unfortunately, the bad luck continues as he’ll be going into Week 3 without a win and without Jayden Daniels. He has Stafford as a replacement, but QB isn’t my only concern for Johny; Marvin Harrison Jr has just 1 catch on the season. This team’s potential is definitely higher than its current rank, but Johny’s going to have to make some moves.

Once again, Rick’s top draft picks failed to score many points at all. So far there have been glaring weaknesses in nearly every position on this team, and it might be too much to fix. Five teams will be missing the playoffs this season, and Rick has a lot of question marks to address after starting 0-2.

200 burger with fries on Rick’s head. With four players landing on the Team of the Week, Hugh’s Heated Team balled out. On top of picking up Mahomes for free to replace the injured Caleb Williams, Brock Bowers scored 27.6 in his long-awaited season debut. It was poor of me to drop Hugh from 1 to 6 after one bad game last week. I apologize.

Bijan and Kenneth Walker were yet again our league’s highest scoring RB duo. Garrett Wilson had another incredible game to show he has what it takes to be a WR1. TE continues to be a concern, though, as both Dalton Schultz and Loveland scored under their projections. On the bright side, Loveland seemed more involved with Case Keenum’s Bears.

Greg had an explosive week after his players racked up plenty of touchdowns to defeat the Dream Dwerkers. Four of his players scored 20+ points, making up for lacking games from Etienne and Irving. The only reason Greg remains at 3 is that Etienne will miss some time due to a hamstring injury. Admittedly, the RB hasn’t been a large factor thus far, but Greg will have to look to the bench or the waiver wire for a new starter.

JSN had another insane game, but Jorge failed to beat Greg after Baker got injured and his FLEX’s combined for only 6.4 points. Luckily for him, Darnold is healthy again and looked in fine form against Washington. Depth is still a real concern for the Dwerkers, though. You can’t rely on just a handful of good performances to carry you to victory every week.

The Little Beauties have crept their way into the top 5 after another solid outing. Luke’s squad is sneakily the second highest scoring team in the league so far, proving that ESPN might’ve known what it was doing when it drafted for him. Davante Adams has taken advantage of Puka’s absence, but it will be interesting to see how Luke’s best player performs going forward.

I gave Quinn the top rank and he failed to crack 100 immediately after. Of course, last week I dropped #1 Hugh to 6th and he then scored 200 points, so clearly I don’t know what I’m doing. After a trade with Camden, Quinn’s new QB Jared Goff should add some much needed points. However, team still has a soft spot at WR and a downgrade from Deebo to Trey Tucker won’t fix that.

Derrick Henry star RB Derrick Henry had another big week, leading Jackson to victory in his must-win matchup with Brady. The team has some great players, but the bench is looking pretty light with Bateman returning to a minor role and Pacheco and Mitchell dealing with injuries. If Jackson could get his hands on another RB or a standout WR for his FLEX, his recent success will continue.

Purdy and CMC keep balling out, and Michael Wilson joined the party with his 25.9 points. Egbuka will be joining Nabers in playing without their starting QBs. After the draft, I thought Kyle’s WR group had massive upside, but we still haven’t seen enough from them to impress me.

Once again, Camden’s team is Josh Allen, James Cook, and that’s pretty much it. He needs his other players to lock in, but a recent trade might have helped him. Swapping Trey Tucker out for Deebo Samuel could prove to be a masterclass. Tucker has had just one big game and will be now competing with Brock Bowers for targets, while Deebo could become the 49ers WR1 if Mike Evans misses time with his rib injury.

Not much has gone right for Brady thus far. Puka has now missed 2 games in a row, and is questionable for his upcoming matchup with Philly. Breece Hall is expected to miss a game with a thigh injury, and Jalen Coker is questionable after picking up his third separate injury in three weeks. With AJ Brown not eligible to come off the IR until Week 6, Brady might need a miracle.

Rick’s moving up! Despite losing to Hugh’s 200 point game, he was able to field a decent team thanks to Tee Higgins and Luther Burden III. Saquon remains a fantasy bust at this point, and the QB situation is murky at best, but Rick is trending in the right direction.

The lowest scorer of the week and new #12 team is Johny’s Finest Team. Achane tore his ACL. The only RBs left on the roster are JCM (7.9 avg pts), Charbonnet (hasn’t played), and Najee Harris (2.9 avg pts). Achane was the one player Johny couldn’t afford to lose, and with him out for the season the team cannot win in their current state. It’s up to Johny to make the changes necessary to revive the squad.

It wasn’t pretty, but thanks to massive games from Bijan and Walker, Last Chance U was able to rally to victory. Despite poor games from key players Parker Washington and Garrett Wilson, Jamo had his first 100 yard game and Loveland’s production is trending in the right direction. Free agents Drake Maye and Ollie Gordon II dazzled on the bench, scoring 26 and 18 respectively.

Jackson didn’t even need Derrick Henry to beat Hugh. Scoring 181.62 thanks in part to CeeDee’s 41.3, Jackson makes it a 3 game winning streak. With Judkins and Odunze finally having big games, this team looks like it could have a hot hand for many weeks to come. The only concern is how Lamar’s injury could impact a team that’s so heavily invested in the Ravens.

The top ranked team gets toppled once again. Despite to loss, Hugh’s squad scored the third highest total. Brock Bowers has scored more than 20 in both of his games so far, Mahomes has proven he can be relied on, and Gibbs is still the fantasy RB1. However, a weakness might emerge in the RB2 spot now that Jaylen Warren will be relinquishing a chunk of his carries to Rico Dowdle.

JSN might not have had a huge game, but he’s still the top player in fantasy so far. With Kyren’s recent performances and Nico Collins back from injury, the Dream Dwerkers’ big three is one to be reckoned with. Price will be on the IR for some time, but RJ Harvey managed to catch the ball ten times from Jorge’s bench and might become a starter should his role in the Bronco’s passing offense continue.

It wasn’t a game to write home about, but Luke was able to muster a win over Rick by a thin margin. David Montgomery hasn’t had a good game since Week 1, and Rashee Rice didn’t play due to a hamstring injury. However, Emanuel Wilson looks like he’ll be the lead back in Seattle for the new few weeks after scoring 27 from 24 touches on Luke’s bench.

Quinn’s now lost two games in a row after being ranked #1. Despite McConkey scoring 0 points due to a reaggravated injury, he still put up over 130 points. Chuba led the way with a standout 25.9 point performance, while the lowest scoring RB on Quinn’s roster not named Josh Jacobs scored 19.1. WR still looks light with both McLaurin and McConkey dealing with an injury, but his trade for Jared Goff definitely looked good after their first game together.

Yikes. Greg’s 102.94 made this the second week already he’s been the lowest scorer. With ETN being placed on the IR, there was more pressure than ever on Love and Irving to perform, but they each scored a measly 6 points. Love is now questionable with an ankle injury again, and although Greg added Blake Corum from the waivers, he may need to find another way to treat his RB problem if he wants to win games.

A win for Kyle last week was a win for my power rankings after he beat Camden’s team, who was ranked one spot below him. His 9ers boys played well, but big games from Tate, Nabers, and Wilson sealed the deal. It might be panic time for Egbuka though. His new QB genuinely sucks and Egbuka only managed to get 2 catches. Kyle needs his other young WRs to keep giving him big games in the meantime.

Camden may have lost, but the Deebo trade aged very well. The WR was one of his top scorers, and once Justin Jefferson is back in the lineup, points should come easy. He definitely should either drop or trade one of his 3 TEs for a RB since he only has 2 on the whole roster and bye week season is upon us.

Puka and Kamara had massive games, but Brady has now lost 3 in a row. Nearly his entire bench is injured, and now Lamar is dealing with what might be a serious ankle injury. It’s gonna take a lot of work for Brady to bounce back, but not all hope is lost if he’s willing to take some risks, especially since everyone’s got a loss.

Rick left two kickers on his bench. One of them scored enough to give him a win over Luke, but instead he’s 0-4. It’s panic time. Saquon, as much as I love him, has been a fantasy bust and is now injured. He’s still got Javonte Williams, who’s been on fire, and Tee Higgins has had some great games lately, but Rick might need to offload a key player just to get a few more scorers in the lineup.
